title: site-copy-ownership-vs-serving-playbook
summary: Working brief: treat the homepage and product pages as a conversion funnel that resolves the common buyer tension: build/own inference vs. buy/serve. Target primary audiences (platform teams, ML/product engineers, security/compliance owners) with distinct hero hooks and product section copy. Includes competitive cues, hero variants, test plan, and metrics.
body:
Context: we repeatedly see two buyer instincts when teams evaluate LLM infrastructure: (1) Build and own inference to control cost and customization, or (2) Buy a managed service to reduce ops burden and accelerate product velocity. Redwood's product truth is that serving is the new leverage point: you can get control + economics + safety without starting from scratch. This brief articulates how that argument should flow across the homepage hero, product landing pages, and three-up value props.

Goals: increase homepage-to-signup conversion by clarifying the play (serve vs own), reduce inbound competitive pricing questions, improve qualified demo requests from platform teams. Expected primary lift: 10–15% higher CTA clicks for platform-oriented copy; better time-to-first-API-call for starter flows.

Audience segmentation and narratives: 
- Platform teams: speak to "predictable throughput and operational consistency". Pain: fragmented endpoints, shadow stacks, unpredictable costs. Proof: Dedicated capacity and routing policies, SLA language, autoscaling stories.
- ML / Product engineers: speak to "fast experimentation and iteration". Pain: slow spin-up, model maintenance overhead, latency surprises. Proof: simple API, model catalog, streaming, KV/prefix cache features.
- Security / Compliance owners: speak to "data isolation and auditability". Pain: regulatory constraints, KMS/HSM needs. Proof: Private deployments, VPC control plane, audit logs.

Voice and tone guidance: clear, engineering-first, pragmatic — avoid marketing hyperbole. Use measurable words (latency ms, cost reduction percentages when available), and concrete primitives (dedicated GPU pools, canary rollouts, token-level breakdown).

Placement strategy: homepage hero = problem framing + one-line value prop + primary CTA for "Get started" and secondary CTA "Compare architectures". Immediately below: three-up value props (Performance, Cost Controls, Reliability & Security) with 1–2 supporting bullets each. Product pages (Runtime, Dedicated, Private, Optimize) link from the three-up. Each product page ends with a short customer story / benchmark snippet and a CTA to request capacity or start a trial.

Anticipated objections and rebuttals (copy-ready): 
- "We can run this ourselves for cheaper" → "Reserved infrastructure often looks cheaper on paper but hides ops, tuning, and regressions. Redwood’s Dedicated combines reserved throughput with runtime optimizations and continuous batching that lower per-token costs and operational risk."
- "What about model fidelity?" → "Rollouts and evals are first-class: pin model versions, A/B, and monitor quality regressions tied to prompt sets."
- "Can we keep data in our network?" → "Yes — VPC/private options with KMS integrations and audit logs are available for enterprise deployments."

Copy hygiene: avoid making quant claims without a pinned benchmark; when we use numbers, link to the bench page. Keep hero lines short (<= 9 words) and subheads 10–14 words.
hero_variants: Serve inference with predictable latency, anywhere you run it.
Get GPU-grade throughput without the ops—hosted, dedicated, or private.
Same API. Safer deployments. Better unit economics.
Ship LLM features with latency SLAs and predictable costs.
Control your inference stack without building it from scratch.
subheads: Unified runtime across hosted, reserved, and private deployments for product teams.
Autoscaling, canaries, and per-route analytics so you can measure cost and quality.
Model catalog plus optimization recommendations that actually reduce token spend.
three_up_value_props: Performance: GPU-optimized serving, KV/prefix caching, and smart batching to hit latency SLOs.
Cost Controls: reserved capacity, intelligent batching and quantization recommendations to lower per-token spend.
Reliability & Security: SLA-backed Dedicated tiers, private VPC deployments, and audit-ready logs.
product_page_outline: Runtime (overview): how the serving runtime works; kernel selection, KV cache, batching; developer quickstart.
Dedicated (overview): reserved pools, autoscaling policy examples, SLA language, pricing hints and commitment levels.
Private (overview): VPC control plane, on-prem option, KMS/HSM integrations, audit and compliance checklist.
Console & Ops: token-level billing, per-route dashboards, rollout controls, tracing hooks.
Optimize: batching/caching suggestions, quantization profiles, cost vs latency tradeoff table.
competitive_notes: Public clouds: strength = scale/availability; weakness = lack of inference primitives (prefix caching, KV) and opinionated runtime tuning. Position Redwood as specialized serving layer with lower TCO for production LLMs.
LLM API providers: strength = simplicity; weakness = limited deployment modes and opaque performance. Emphasize transparent benchmarks and choice of deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private).

Inference infra vendors/open-source runtimes: strength = control; weakness = ops bill and fragmentation. Position Redwood as the middle ground: control without building. Provide cost-model calculator to rebut \"we can do this cheaper\" claims.
a_b_test_hypotheses: H1: Platform-centric hero (\"predictable throughput\") will increase demo requests from platform teams by 20% vs generic hero.
H2: Adding an explicit cost-control triad under the hero will reduce pricing-related support questions by 25%.
H3: A secondary CTA to \"Compare architectures\" will improve trial-to-paid conversion among mid-market accounts by surfacing Dedicated benefits earlier.
primary_metrics: New signups that call themselves \"platform\" or \"infra\" in onboarding - target +18%
next_steps: Lock 6 hero variants into Optimizely and run 2-week test: platform-hero vs generic-hero.
Create 3 product-page experiments (Runtime, Dedicated, Private) with new outline and bench snippets.
Ask Applied ML to produce 2 short benchmark blurbs (p99 latency, tokens/sec) we can cite on pages.
Design a headline visual showing \"same API across environments\" (one-liner + diagram) for hero.
Sync with Solutions and Sales to update the competitive battlecard with rebuttals from this doc.
